data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 shares mechanism with SRC_005 because both target the same false-green risk: an endpoint identity comparison that is silently weakened to a partial or homogeneous match. SRC_003's mechanism is a rubric: eval form declaring the school-to-seat homogenization mutation as forbidden when no test provides a mismatched endpoint under the same school ID. SRC_005's mechanism is a program: eval form that mutates the endpoint identity comparison to ignore drift and asserts a typed lease-mismatch code is returned. The shared mechanism is the mutation class — both forbid weakening the endpoint identity comparison to ignore a discriminating field (school ID vs. full endpoint identity in SRC_003; drift field vs. full endpoint identity in SRC_005). The difference is enforcement: rubric: marking (SRC_003) vs. program: assertion (SRC_005), but the underlying attack vector — identity homogenization — is identical. This claim is REFUTED IF the identity comparison in SRC_003 (school-to-seat binding using school ID as partial key) operates on a different comparison axis than SRC_005 (lease binding using endpoint drift field), such that no single mutation class covers both, meaning the mechanism is not shared but merely analogous.
